verdict.explanation: Round-5 grade policy (Claude review): when ANY API the mod calls resolves to a catalog entry with a blank ps5_runtime_status, NO verdict is possible, so the grade is 'unknown - runtime status not filled'. The mod's 9 core runtime APIs (RegisterKeyBind, ExecuteInGameThread, StaticFindObject, ...) are all still blank (599/599 merged catalog entries), so no compatibility claim can be made. The six Key.* keyboard keybind constants stay detected in the pc_only_input bucket and are now listed as a KNOWN PS5 DIFFERENCE inside this unknown result -- a PC-only keyboard dependency no longer upgrades the grade to partly-compatible. This reverses the round-4 behavior, which graded partly-compatible on the strength of the keyboard difference while the rest was unverifiable.

catalog_entry.name: Key
catalog_entry.notes: TYPE entry for the global 'Key' constant table (same entry style as FName/FString types; no methods, only constants). Values are Windows VK_* codes (Input::Key enum, deps/first/Input/include/Input/KeyDef.hpp: e.g. RETURN=0x0D, LEFT_ARROW=0x25, UP_ARROW=0x26, F7=0x76) cast to uint32_t. Constants are pure integers and readable in any Lua state without a game (needs_live_game=false), but every value denotes a PC keyboard/mouse key that has no PS5 equivalent to press: a Key.* keybind dependency needs translation to a controller input (current approach: PS5Pad.ini chord mapping, e.g. L3+R3 = F7). Identical 165-constant list verified byte-for-byte between the port (src/Mod/LuaMod.cpp:448-614) and upstream (src/Mod/LuaMod.cpp:440-606). Source attribution: verified against port (port citations retained as secondary); upstream reference: src/Mod/LuaMod.cpp:438-606 (register_input_globals)

pc_only_input.suggestion: keyboard keybinds -> needs runtime/config controller mapping on PS5 (PS5 has no keyboard; map controller chords, e.g. L3+R3 = F7, via PS5Pad.ini or an equivalent runtime translation layer)
